name: Omid Kordestani
current_role: Chair of the Board, Pearson plc (since 2022); non-executive director, Klarna Group
profile: Tehran-born Iranian-American executive who ran Google's worldwide sales and business operations from 1999 to 2009 (and returned as Chief Business Officer 2014-15), building the wealth tied to his early Alphabet stock. He was later executive chairman of Twitter (2015-2020) and has chaired education company Pearson since 2022.
interesting_fact: Before Google he ran OEM sales and business development at Netscape; at Google he built the global sales organisation that turned search ads into the company's revenue engine. Time named him one of its 100 people who shape our world in 2006.
deep_cut_fact: He moved to San Jose after his father died in 1976, graduated from Buchser High School in Santa Clara (1980), studied electrical engineering at San Jose State and worked as an engineer at Hewlett-Packard before his 1991 Stanford MBA.
notes: Best route is via Pearson's corporate media team (corporate/financial media contacts listed on the IR contacts page; addresses obfuscated there). Co-founded the PARSA Community Foundation for the Iranian-American community. Pearson confirmed him as chair in a Sept 2026 board announcement.

name: Rajju Shroff
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, UPL Ltd (since Dec 2022)
profile: Rajnikant 'Rajju' Shroff founded Mumbai-based UPL in 1969 to make red phosphorus and built it over 50+ years as chairman and MD into one of the world's largest crop-protection companies, especially after the $4.2bn Arysta LifeScience deal in 2018. He stepped down at 90 in Dec 2022; son Jai Shroff is now chairman and group CEO.
interesting_fact: UPL began in 1969 producing red phosphorus, which Shroff pioneered making in India. He was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2021 and Mexico's Order of the Aztec Eagle in 2018.
deep_cut_fact: A Bombay University chemistry graduate from a Kutch entrepreneurial family, in 1957 he developed a new process for making mercury salts at a UK plant, and a British company paid him royalties for it, which was rare for an Indian chemist at the time.
notes: Now about 93 and retired to focus on social causes; UPL lists upl@uniphos.com for corporate-affairs enquiries. Son Jai Shroff (chairman/CEO) is the active public face.

name: Terry Leprino
current_role: President, Leprino Foods Company Foundation; board director and co-owner, Leprino Foods (Denver)
profile: Terry Leprino and her sister Gina Vecchiarelli inherited about 90% of Denver-based Leprino Foods, the world's largest mozzarella maker (est. $3.6bn revenue; supplies Domino's, Pizza Hut, Papa John's), after their father James Leprino died in June 2025. She spent a decade as the company's marketing director, sits on its board and now leads the corporate foundation.
interesting_fact: Leprino Foods, founded by her grandfather in 1950, makes more than 1 billion pounds of cheese a year; her father pioneered the technology to make pizza cheese at industrial scale.
deep_cut_fact: She holds a bachelor's from Arizona State and a master's in biblical counseling from Colorado Christian University, where she has served as a trustee for over a decade. She also sits on the board of the Issachar Urban Leadership Center.
notes: Very private family business with no named PR contact. The media centre directs press to Corporate Communications by phone, and the contact form has a 'Media' option. The CCU trustee bio URL came up in search results but returned 404 when fetched directly.

name: Philippe Benacin
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Interparfums SA (Paris); Vice Chairman and President, Inter Parfums, Inc. (Nasdaq: IPAR)
profile: French entrepreneur who co-founded fragrance maker Interparfums in 1982 with Jean Madar, right after business school (ESSEC, 1983), after learning in class how high fragrance-industry margins were. Listed on Nasdaq in 1988 at a ~$4m valuation, the group now makes licensed perfumes for brands such as Jimmy Choo, Montblanc, Coach, Lacoste and Moncler. Benacin runs the European business, about two thirds of sales.
interesting_fact: He told Journal du Luxe that he got into licensing 'largely by chance': the first licence came in 1990, and a 1993 Burberry licence became the springboard for growth. He was inducted into The Fragrance Foundation Hall of Fame in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: Asked in a March 2026 interview what he is proudest of at Interparfums, he chose not a brand but its 'communauté d'esprit', the team's shared spirit. In the same interview he argued that Gen Z is very attached to niche perfume.

public_contacts.value: The Equity Group (Devin Sullivan), investor relations for Inter Parfums, Inc.

notes: Gives interviews to the French luxury and beauty trade press (Journal du Luxe, Premium Beauty News). For the French side, the Interparfums Finance contact page is the best route; the US IR agency is The Equity Group.

name: Alexander Rinke
profile: German entrepreneur who co-founded process-mining and 'process intelligence' software company Celonis in 2011 with fellow Munich students Bastian Nominacher and Martin Klenk. Celonis was valued at $13bn in 2022, and Rinke owns about 15%. As co-CEO he is now pitching Celonis as the data layer for enterprise AI, unveiling the Celonis Context Model in 2026.
interesting_fact: Celonis was bootstrapped at first because investors found process mining too hard to understand. To get past gatekeepers, the founders hand-wrote about 1,500 letters to CEOs, which helped land Siemens as a customer.
deep_cut_fact: Celonis began with a 2011 student-consultancy (Academy Consult) IT job at broadcaster Bayerischer Rundfunk. The trio wrote simple software to measure gaps between timestamps and showed on a few A4 printouts how processes taking up to five days could be cut to hours.
notes: Very media-accessible: he speaks at WEF Davos and Web Summit and appears on tech podcasts. Celonis PR (press@celonis.com) handles interview and meeting requests. His AI/data-infrastructure angle fits a data-centre podcast.

name: Hope van Beuren
current_role: Founder and Chair Emerita, van Beuren Charitable Foundation (Newport, RI)
profile: Hope Hill 'Happy' van Beuren is a Campbell Soup heiress and granddaughter of John T. Dorrance, who invented the condensed-soup process. Forbes put her net worth at about $1.1bn (last listed 2011). With her late husband John A. 'Archie' van Beuren she founded the van Beuren Charitable Foundation in 1986, which focuses on the Newport, Rhode Island region.
interesting_fact: The van Beuren Charitable Foundation she co-founded in 1986 says it has given more than $150 million to the Newport region.
deep_cut_fact: Known as 'Happy', she says the foundation's guiding principles were formed 'around the family kitchen table': family involvement, firsthand knowledge of the community, and acting with integrity, intelligence and imagination.

public_contacts.value: elynn@vbcfoundation.org (Elizabeth R. Lynn, Executive Director, van Beuren Charitable Foundation)

notes: Elderly (engaged in 1954) and very private. Alive status is inferred: the foundation's current site lists her as Founder and Chair Emerita, and I found no obituary, but I couldn't confirm it independently. Contact only via the foundation's executive director. Low fit for an energy/data-centre podcast.

name: Pan Xueping
current_role: Chairman, Jiangsu Jinsheng Industry (金昇实业) and Saurer Intelligent Technology (卓郎智能, SSE: 600545)
profile: Pan Xueping (潘雪平) founded Changzhou-based Jiangsu Jinsheng Industry in 2000. In 2013 Jinsheng bought Oerlikon's natural-fibre and textile-components businesses (deal value about CHF 650m) and revived the historic Swiss Saurer brand. Pan chairs Shanghai-listed Saurer Intelligent Technology and is vice-president of China's textile machinery and textile engineering associations.
interesting_fact: Jinsheng's 2013 purchase of Oerlikon's textile units brought back the 160-year-old Swiss Saurer name. Pan said the new Saurer would be run operationally from Wattwil, Switzerland and financially from Shanghai.
deep_cut_fact: A textile-machinery engineer by background, before founding Jinsheng he ran a spinning-ring (钢领) factory at Pacific Group's Shanghai textile-parts works, then led the Jintan Textile Machinery Plant and was CEO of a Swiss spinning group's front-end spinning division.
notes: Low public profile in English-language media. Name in Chinese: 潘雪平; Hurun's 'Jinsheng' is 金昇. Jinsheng also has large textile operations in Xinjiang (Litai Silk Road), a possibly sensitive topic. Best route is Saurer IR.

name: Zhu Wei
current_role: Co-founder and long-time shareholder of Changxin Bochuang Technology (长芯博创, SZSE: 300548, formerly Broadex Technologies). He was chairman/GM until 2022; the current chairman is Zhuang Dan.
profile: Most likely ZHU WEI (朱伟), a US-citizen photonics scientist born in 1963 who co-founded Jiaxing-based optical-communications component maker Broadex Technologies in 2003 and chaired it from 2010. In 2022 he planned a share transfer and change of control, and the company was renamed Changxin Bochuang in 2025. The AI-driven boom in optical-module stocks lifted his stake's value.
interesting_fact: Before founding Broadex he spent about a decade as a researcher at AT&T Bell Labs (1993-96) and Lucent Bell Labs (1996-2002), then at Agere Systems.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a PhD in solid-state science from Penn State, was a visiting assistant professor of materials science at North Carolina State (1990-93), and at the same time was a part-time visiting researcher at Italy's CSM SpA.
notes: Identity is inferred, not confirmed by the list: the input gives only 'telecommunication', US nationality and Hurun China 2020, which match the Broadex founder (a US national, controlling shareholder in 2020). His current role after the 2022 change of control is unverified, and the IR email is from the 2020 annual report. Optical interconnects fit a data-centre podcast well.

name: Kostyantin Zhevago
current_role: Major shareholder of Ferrexpo plc (former executive director, 2008-2019); owner of FC Vorskla Poltava
profile: Ukrainian businessman and former MP (1998-2019) whose fortune comes mainly from his stake in London-listed iron-ore pellet producer Ferrexpo, which runs mines in Poltava region. He stepped down as executive director in 2019. He faces several Ukrainian criminal cases and 2025 sanctions, all of which he denies, and lives outside Ukraine; France refused extradition in 2023.
interesting_fact: Taking Ferrexpo public on the London Stock Exchange's main market in 2007 made him the first Ukrainian billionaire to list a company publicly.
deep_cut_fact: He was born in 1974 in Iultin, a remote Arctic mining settlement in Chukotka, and grew up in Dniprorudne in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region. He later earned a PhD in economics (2003) from Kyiv National Economic University.
notes: High-risk outreach target: Ukrainian criminal cases, presidential sanctions (2025) and a seizure order on his Ferrexpo shares. He holds no executive role, and I found no published personal or office contact. Ferrexpo's IR represents the company, not him. Recommend skipping or handling with legal caution.

name: Stanley Tang
current_role: Co-founder and Head of DoorDash Labs, DoorDash (also a director)
profile: Hong Kong-raised (born 1992 in Sendai, Japan), Stanford computer-science graduate who co-founded DoorDash in 2013 with Tony Xu, Andy Fang and Evan Moore. He owns about 4% of the company, which listed on the NYSE in December 2020. He now runs DoorDash Labs, the company's autonomy and robotics unit, which launched the 'Dot' delivery robot in 2025.
interesting_fact: He led the 2025 unveiling of Dot, DoorDash's in-house autonomous delivery robot, which can travel on roads, bike lanes and sidewalks at up to 20 mph. DoorDash says it was tested over millions of simulated and real-world miles.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager in Hong Kong he wrote 'eMillions: Behind-the-Scenes Stories of 14 Internet Millionaires', interviewing online entrepreneurs from age 14. He expected the project to take three months; it took 15.
notes: Strong fit for a robotics, autonomy and AI angle. Go through DoorDash press (press@doordash.com) and mention DoorDash Labs/Dot. Some 2026 sources call him Chief Product Officer, so confirm his exact title.

name: Ivan Streshinsky
current_role: Shareholder (~5%) in USM Holding; former CEO of USM (stepped down in 2022)
profile: Russian lawyer-turned-executive who worked for Alisher Usmanov from 2006, first as CEO of Gazmetall and from 2012 as head of USM Holding, the group behind Metalloinvest, MegaFon and AliExpress Russia. Usmanov gave him 3% of USM in 2014 and 2% more in 2021. He resigned as USM CEO in 2022 to avoid Western sanctions.
interesting_fact: Before joining Usmanov he provided legal support on corporate transactions for billionaire Vasily Anisimov.
deep_cut_fact: He created the rock band ISB, which released its first album, 'Runaway', in 2020.
notes: On the US OFAC SDN list (designated in 2023 under EO 14024). A US-based journalist should get legal advice before any dealings. I found no published personal or office contact; USM is not an appropriate route. Recommend skipping.

name: Pradip Burman
current_role: Chairman, Mobius Foundation and Ayurvet Ltd; Burman family shareholder in Dabur India
profile: MIT-trained mechanical engineer and great-grandson of Dabur founder Dr S.K. Burman, whose wealth comes from his family's stake in Ayurvedic consumer-goods group Dabur. As a Dabur executive he launched veterinary herbal-products business Ayurvet, which he still chairs. Since 2015 his Mobius Foundation has focused on sustainability education, population stabilisation and renewable energy.
interesting_fact: His Mobius Foundation launched the World Environment School in Coorg, billed as India's first environment-focused school, on about 100 acres in the Western Ghats with support from the UK's Whitgift School.
deep_cut_fact: His MIT mechanical-engineering graduation project was a sonic aid for the visually impaired that used ultrasonic waves to detect obstacles. He named his foundation after mathematician August Möbius, because the Möbius strip symbolises balance and union.
notes: Born around 1942; alive status is presumed from recent foundation activity, and I found no obituary. He is also a trustee of Climate Reality Project India, which makes the sustainability and renewables angle a natural hook. I found no verified published email; the Mobius Foundation site (mobiusfoundation.org) did not load when checked. Approach via the foundation.
